state:
**Goal `ldap`, Stage 10 (the feature proofs) is under way.** Stages 1 to 5 and 7 to 9 are done; Stage 4 lacks only a CA a program supplies, and Stage 6 lacks only wiring the schema into the readers. `Core\Ldap`, `Core\Ldap\Filter`, `Core\Ldap\Dn`, `Core\Ldap\Sid`, `Core\Ldap\Ad` and `Core\Ldap\Change` owe nothing: every member has an `about.md`, three examples, an attack, a bench with a recorded figure in `docs/perf/members.ndjson`, and a `covers:` marker on a Rust test (and on a `.nvst` case for an instance member).

**Every flag reader is a feature that owes every proof.** `data/proofs/policy.json` has no exclusion by kind, and a skip entry is only for a reason a proof cannot exist, so the 24 features of `Core\Ldap\Ad\AccountFlags` and the 9 of `Core\Ldap\Ad\GroupType` each owe an `about.md`, three examples, an attack and a bench. Their tests are done: `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/ldap/flags.rs`' unit test calls every member through `call`, and three `.nvst` cases carry the Novis-side markers. **No program can build a flag object without a live entry**: the classes have no constructor, only `Entry::accountFlags` and `Entry::groupType` return one. So their examples, attacks and benches wait for the `samba-ad` proof footing too, with `Connection`, `Entries`, `Entry` and `Changes`.

**A filter nests at most 100 levels** (`rule:core-classes/ldap-filter-is-a-value`, `nvs_ldap::MAX_FILTER_DEPTH`). `Filter::all` and `any` take their filters as separate arguments, so a list is passed as `...$list`.

**How proofs run with no server today**, on `Core\Mail::send`'s footing: the root `nvs.toml` has an `[ldap.corp]` block at `ldaps://127.0.0.1:1`, a closed port, and one `[[app]] entry` per proof program that needs a grant. In a proof program, a catch variable or a `var` reused in one file with another type does not compile (E0406): name each `LogicError` catch `$refusal` and each `Throwable` catch `$error`, and give every `var` in a file its own name. An instance member's `covers:` line in a `.nvst` case goes at the end of the `--FILE--` block, so no line number moves.

next.title: the feature proofs, the `samba-ad` footing the user decided on

items.text: **A proof program can name the `samba-ad` service it needs** (`rule:testing/feature-proofs`, the user's decision in the Backlog's first item): a `// requires: samba-ad` marker beside the two at `tools/nv/proofs/run.ts:69`, which runs `docker compose up -d --wait samba-ad` once before the first selected program that carries it, the way `tools/nv/cmd/db-matrix.ts:346` does, and fails that program with a plain message when Docker is absent. Programs without the marker never touch Docker.

**A seed step writes one fixed set of users and groups into the empty `EXAMPLE.TEST` domain** (`tests/db/compose.yaml:375`), so every `.out` is stable. It is idempotent, and the names are neutral (`Staff`, `Shop`), never a reporter's.

**The root `nvs.toml`'s `[ldap.corp]` points at the container's LDAPS port with the test CA** (the block is at line 2719 of the root file; the service is `tests/db/compose.yaml:375`), and the `Core\Ldap::connect` and `open` examples that print the closed-port error are rewritten to show a real sign-in, then re-blessed.

backlog: **Decided by the user: `Connection`, `Entries`, `Entry`, `Changes` and the two flag classes prove themselves against the real `samba-ad` service**, never through a skip entry in `data/proofs/policy.json`. After the footing lands, each class gets its `about.md`, examples, attack and bench (`docs/examples/core/Ldap-Ad-AccountFlags/`, `docs/examples/core/Ldap-Ad-GroupType/` and their twins).

`Ad::memberOf` with a string does not check that the string is a DN: `memberOf('not a DN')` returns `(memberOf=not a DN)`, which matches nothing (`crates/nvs-stdlib/src/ldap/search.rs`, `nvs_core_ldap_ad_member_of`).
Every `Dn` member parses the slot text again (`crates/nvs-stdlib/src/ldap/dn.rs`' module doc), so walking up an n-level DN with `parent` is O(n²).
`nv try` does not apply an `[[app]]` grant from the root `nvs.toml`, so a probe of a granted member needs `nv proofs --bless` instead (`tools/nv/cmd/try.ts`).
Stage 4: a CA a program supplies to `Ldap::open` (`docs/agent/goals/ldap.md`).
Stage 6: wiring the schema into the readers (`crates/nvs-ldap/src/schema.rs`).
